meta.name: printed-polymer fatigue (S-N) registry
meta.schema_kind_note: NOT a tools/materials.py material record — a sidecar table. materials.py load_all() skips any file whose meta.schema_kind is not 'material_record'.
meta.why_separate_file: tools/materials/<key>.json are the unified material records (owned elsewhere); this file adds ONLY the fatigue-curve layer and its provenance. It never overrides a record — the runner reads E/UTS from tools/materials.py and the S-N curve from here.
meta.scope: FDM/FFF-PRINTED specimens only. Bulk/injection-moulded polymer S-N data is NOT admitted: printed parts fail by layer debonding and inter-bead void growth, mechanisms absent from bulk specimens (the same review that reports FDM ABS at 6.0e4 cycles reports injection-moulded ABS at 6.0e6 cycles for the SAME 10 MPa — a 100x gap).
meta.blunt_validity_statement: This is a COMPARATIVE / SCREENING tool, not a certification basis. Printed-part fatigue is dominated by layer adhesion, raster geometry and process defects; published scatter for printed PLA spans a factor of 3.7x to 90x in LIFE between the 10% and 90% survival curves (the runner recomputes that band from source_table every run: T_life = T_sigma^k). Use it to rank design variants and to reject obviously-overstressed features, never to certify a cycle count.

status_values.measured: at least two independent printed-specimen datasets with usable S-N parameters that agree within the published scatter; the runner will return a life number
status_values.insufficient: printed data exists but is not enough to fit a defensible curve (too few decades, no published coefficients, or a single lineage); the runner REFUSES and says so
status_values.unknown: no printed-specimen fatigue data found; the runner REFUSES and says so

policy.refusal_rule: A material whose status is not 'measured' gets NO life number. Substituting bulk-polymer data would be a fabricated answer, so the runner names the material, the status and the reason instead.
policy.orientation_rule: Every curve here is for IN-PLANE (flat on the build plate, load in the layer plane) specimens. ACROSS-LAYER (Z, load normal to the layers) fatigue of printed polymers is UNKNOWN — no S-N dataset was found for any material in this registry (2026-07-30). The runner refuses `load_orientation: across_layer` rather than applying the static z_vs_xy_strength_ratio knockdown, because a static strength ratio is not a fatigue-slope ratio and nothing measured supports the substitution.

PLA.confidence_basis: Two independent peer-reviewed printed-PLA axial-fatigue datasets (different printers, filament suppliers, raster angles, load ratios and years) agree to 0.4% on the Basquin coefficient A and to within 21% on the R=-1-equivalent endurance amplitude at 2e6 cycles — good agreement for polymer fatigue, whose own within-study 90/10 scatter is larger than that. Downgraded from High because: no dataset exceeds 2e6 cycles, no across-layer data exists, and infill/wall counts differ from typical print settings.
PLA.sigma_uts_source: LOWEST measured printed UTS of the three raster angles in Ezeh & Susmel 2019 (42.6 / 40.9 / 42.5 MPa at theta_p = 0/30/45 deg). Deliberately NOT tools/materials/pla.json mechanical.ultimate_mpa = 55.0, which is datasheet-class and would make both the design curve (0.1 x UTS) and any Goodman correction UNCONSERVATIVE — see conflicts[0].

design.derivation: Ezeh & Susmel 2019 eq. (5)-(6), the paper's OWN recommended unifying design curve for AM PLA at 100% infill: negative inverse slope k = 5.5 and endurance limit sigma_MAX = 0.10 x sigma_UTS at N_ref = 2e6 cycles, expressed in MAXIMUM stress in the cycle. sigma_at_n_ref_mpa = 0.10 x 40.9 = 4.09 MPa. Basquin form sigma_max = a * N^b with b = -1/k = -0.181818..., a = 4.09 * (2e6)^(1/5.5) = 57.195929924926574 MPa (stored to full binary64 precision so a consumer can re-derive it exactly).
design.note: DEFAULT curve. Expressed in MAX stress on purpose: Ezeh & Susmel found that for AM PLA the maximum stress in the cycle already absorbs the mean-stress effect (their Fig. 8a: the 2e6-cycle endurance limit in sigma_MAX is 9.5 MPa +-2SD across R = -1, -0.5, 0 and +0.3). Applying Goodman/Gerber ON TOP of this curve double-counts the mean stress; the runner refuses that combination.

median.derivation: Ezeh & Susmel 2019 Table 1, theta_p = 0 deg, R = -1 (15 specimens): k = 7.7, sigma_A,50% = 10.4 MPa at N_ref = 2e6, T_sigma = 1.185. Basquin sigma_a = a * N^b with b = -1/k = -0.129870..., a = 10.4 * (2e6)^(1/7.7) = 68.44613399542558 MPa (stored to full binary64 precision).
median.note: MEDIAN curve — by construction 50% of specimens fail BEFORE this life. Never a default. Fully-reversed (R = -1) basis, so a mean-stress correction (goodman|gerber) is REQUIRED for any spectrum with sigma_m != 0.
median.corroboration: Independent fit from source[1] (different lab/printer/year, smooth ASTM D638-I specimens, R = 0.05, 5 Hz): sigma_a = 68.159 * N^-0.161, R^2 = 0.991. Coefficient A agrees to 0.42% (68.159 vs 68.446 MPa); exponent b differs 24% (-0.161 vs -0.12987), which is inside the source-0 slope spread (k = 4.3 .. 8.9 across its 12 configurations, i.e. b = -0.1124 .. -0.2326). At 2e6 cycles source[1] gives sigma_a = 6.593 MPa at R = 0.05; Goodman-corrected to R = -1 (its own measured UTS 37.23 MPa) that is 8.197 MPa vs this curve's 10.4 MPa — 21% apart, well inside the 90/10 scatter band (3.7x in life for this configuration).

life_scatter.note: T_sigma is the 90%/10%-survival ratio of the endurance STRESS; the corresponding LIFE band is T_sigma^k, computed per configuration. The runner recomputes min/max over source_table every run and quotes it in the receipt (measured 2026-07-30: 3.70x best, 90.39x worst).

source_table.description: Ezeh & Susmel 2019 Table 1 verbatim: median (PS=50%) S-N curves. Columns [theta_p_deg, sigma_uts_mpa, n_specimens, r_ratio, k, sigma_a_50_mpa_at_2e6, t_sigma].

test_conditions.specimen: FFF-printed dog-bone, flat on the build plate, 100% infill
test_conditions.orientation: in-plane (load in the layer plane); raster angles 0 / 30 / 45 deg
test_conditions.n_specimens: 143 (source[0], >= 8 per configuration per JSME practice) + 22 (source[1] smooth+notched)

sources.citation: O.H. Ezeh, L. Susmel, 'Fatigue strength of additively manufactured polylactide (PLA): effect of raster angle and non-zero mean stresses', International Journal of Fatigue 126 (2019) 319-326
sources.read: full text (open accepted manuscript, Table 1 + eqs. 5-6 transcribed)

sources.role: independent corroboration of the median curve
sources.citation: 'Fatigue Life Assessment of Notched PLA Manufactured Using FDM 3D-Printing Technique', Polymers 18(1):1 (2026)

sources.role: conflicting datum, kept as data (see conflicts[1])
sources.citation: 'Modeling of Effect of Infill Density Percentage on Rotating Bending Fatigue Behavior of Additive-Manufactured PLA Polymers', Polymers (2024)
sources.key_numbers: Rotating bending, R=-1, 100 Hz. N = 10^CB1 * sigma^-CB2 (sigma in MPa); 100% infill CB1=9.974 CB2=3.3825 (R^2 0.999) -> equivalent Basquin a = 889 MPa, b = -0.2956. Mean life at sigma_a=14 MPa: 25% infill 30275; 50% 236585; 75% 878184; 100% 1262213 cycles. No measured UTS reported.

sources.citation: 'Experimental fatigue dataset for additive-manufactured 3D-printed PLA biomaterials under fully-reversed rotating-bending loadings', Data in Brief
sources.read: full text via PMC (article only; the numeric tables live in the Mendeley deposit)
sources.key_numbers: 2.5-17.5 MPa amplitude, R=-1, 100 Hz, horizontal print, 60% rectangular infill, ~400 to 1.5e6 cycles (runout). Authors explicitly leave the Basquin fit as future work. Raw data: Mendeley DOI 10.17632/gyxsn7wg6c.1.

conflicts.field: sigma_uts_mpa used for the design curve and for Goodman/Gerber
conflicts.note: The three fatigue studies measured 37.23 / 40.9 / 42.5 / 42.6 MPa on their OWN printed specimens. Using 55 MPa would raise the design endurance from 4.09 to 5.5 MPa (+34%) and soften every Goodman correction — unconservative in both places. This file keeps the measured printed value and does NOT edit the material record.

conflicts.field: S-N slope and level, axial vs rotating-bending
conflicts.other_value: rotating bending, source 2: N = 10^9.974 sigma^-3.3825 at 100% infill
conflicts.note: At sigma_a = 14 MPa source 2 reports 1.25e6 cycles; the canonical median curve gives 2.03e5 — a 6.2x life gap, and the slopes differ sharply (b -0.2956 vs -0.1299), so the gap widens at lower stress. NOT averaged. Axial is canonical because (a) a bending gradient stresses only the surface fibres, systematically over-reporting fatigue strength relative to the uniform axial stress that an FEA von Mises field represents; (b) source 2 reports no measured UTS, so its data cannot be mean-stress-normalised; (c) 100 Hz on a polymer risks hysteretic self-heating, which sources 0 and 1 avoid at 5-10 Hz. The conflict is recorded, not resolved by averaging.

gaps_unknowns: ACROSS-LAYER (Z) fatigue: NO printed-PLA S-N data found (2026-07-30). The runner refuses across-layer requests instead of knocking down the in-plane curve by the static z_vs_xy ratio.

NOTHING beyond 2e6 cycles: both canonical sources stop at their runout. Any block whose predicted life exceeds 2e6 is EXTRAPOLATION and is flagged as such in the receipt; there is no evidence of a true endurance limit (fatigue limit) for printed PLA.
INFILL: the canonical curves are 100%-infill. Source 2 shows life falling ~40x from 100% to 25% infill at the same nominal stress — sparse-infill parts are NOT covered by this curve.
TEMPERATURE: all data is room-temperature. PLA's Tg is ~60 C and softening_c is 55 C (tools/materials/pla.json); no elevated-temperature printed-PLA S-N data was found.
FREQUENCY / self-heating: sources 0-1 used 5-10 Hz. Nothing here covers the loading rate of, say, a vibrating bracket at 100+ Hz.
VARIABLE-AMPLITUDE validation: Miner's linear rule is APPLIED here but has NOT been validated against a variable-amplitude printed-polymer test in any source found. Sequence effects are unmodelled.
ENVIRONMENT: dry, unaged specimens only. PLA hydrolyses; no wet or aged printed-PLA fatigue data found.

PETG.refusal_reason: Only ONE printed-PETG fatigue study was located, its numeric S-N parameters are behind a paywall, and the reported lives top out around 2e4 cycles (60-90% of UTS) — under two decades of life, no published Basquin coefficients, single lineage. Fitting a curve from that would be an invention, so no life number is returned for PETG.
what_exists: Tensile-tensile fatigue at R = 0.1 on FFF PETG at 90/80/70/60% of UTS, three raster orientations; the longest life reported is ~2e4 cycles at 60% UTS (diagonal orientation). Ranking by orientation is reported; coefficients are not.
A 2023 review states that for PETG 45-deg rasters perform best at low stress amplitude while 0-deg rasters win at high amplitude — a qualitative ordering, not a curve.

sources.read: search snippet only — the publisher returned HTTP 403 to direct fetch (2026-07-30)

PETG.what_would_change_this: A printed-PETG dataset covering >= 3 decades of life with published S-N coefficients and a measured specimen UTS, from a second independent lab.

ABS.refusal_reason: The only printed-ABS fatigue numbers located come from one review lineage and amount to a single (stress, life) pair plus a raster-orientation ranking — not enough points to fit a slope, and no independent corroboration. No life number is returned for ABS.
what_exists: FDM ABS: ~6.0e4 cycles at 10 MPa, versus ~6.0e6 cycles for injection-moulded ABS at the same stress (a 100x printed-vs-bulk penalty — the single most useful number here, and the reason this registry refuses bulk substitutes).
Ziemian et al.: longitudinal (0 deg) and default (+45/-45 deg) rasters outlast diagonal (45 deg) and transverse (90 deg) for ABS.

sources.citation: 'Fatigue behaviour of FDM-3D printed polymers, polymeric composites and architected cellular materials', International Journal of Fatigue 145 (2021) 106106

ABS.what_would_change_this: A printed-ABS S-N dataset with >= 4 stress levels, replicates, a measured UTS and published coefficients, corroborated by a second lab.

ASA.refusal_reason: No printed-ASA fatigue (S-N) dataset located (2026-07-30). One 2026 FFF characterisation paper covering ASA / Nylon 12 / PC / PC-ABS was found by title but its full text could not be retrieved (PMC returned a CAPTCHA challenge), so nothing from it is recorded here.

TPU95A.refusal_reason: No printed-TPU S-N dataset located (2026-07-30). Elastomer fatigue is additionally dominated by hysteretic self-heating and Mullins softening, which a linear-elastic stress-life model does not represent at all — even good data would not make this runner applicable without a hyperelastic stress input.

goodman.formula: sigma_ar = sigma_a / (1 - sigma_m / sigma_uts)  for sigma_m > 0; sigma_ar = sigma_a for sigma_m <= 0
goodman.citation: Modified Goodman line, standard stress-life practice (Shigley's Mechanical Engineering Design, ch. 6; ASTM E1823 terminology). The compressive-mean branch is deliberately NON-beneficial: taking credit for compressive mean stress is unconservative and unvalidated for printed polymers.

gerber.formula: sigma_ar = sigma_a / (1 - (sigma_m / sigma_uts)^2)  for sigma_m > 0; sigma_ar = sigma_a for sigma_m <= 0
gerber.citation: Gerber parabola, standard stress-life practice (Shigley's Mechanical Engineering Design, ch. 6). Less conservative than Goodman.

intrinsic.formula: sigma_eff = sigma_max = sigma_m + sigma_a, used directly against a max-stress S-N curve
intrinsic.citation: Ezeh & Susmel 2019 section 4.2 / Fig. 8a: for AM PLA the endurance limit expressed in MAXIMUM cycle stress is invariant (9.5 MPa +- 2SD) across R = -1 .. +0.3, i.e. the maximum stress already carries the mean-stress effect. This is the ONLY mean-stress treatment in this file that was validated on printed specimens.

damage_rule.name: Palmgren-Miner linear damage accumulation
damage_rule.formula: D = sum_i (n_i / N_i); failure predicted at D = 1
damage_rule.citation: M.A. Miner, 'Cumulative damage in fatigue', J. Appl. Mech. 12 (1945) A159-A164; A. Palmgren (1924).
damage_rule.note: No variable-amplitude printed-polymer validation was found. Miner ignores load-sequence effects; measured D at failure for polymers commonly lands between 0.3 and 2. Treat D = 1 as a nominal threshold, not a proven one.
